input.quote: 11.5 Special, Indirect, and Other Losses. EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8], (C) AS PROVIDED UNDER [***] AND (D) TO THE EXTENT ANY SUCH DAMAGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE PAID TO A THIRD PARTY AS PART OF A CLAIM FOR WHICH A PARTY PROVIDES INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS ARTICLE 11, NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
input.rationale: Section 11.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision. It is mutual and delivers the exclusion-of-damages limb of the rule, with carve-outs that already satisfy the fallback carve-out list (fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence; Article 9 confidentiality; Section 5.8 exclusivity; and indemnified Third Party Claims under Article 11). However, searches for "aggregate liability", "total liability", "exceed" and "liability" confirm that no aggregate monetary cap exists anywhere in the Agreement (Article 11 otherwise covers only indemnity mechanics and insurance limits, and Articles 6, 10, 12 and 13 contain none). Both parties therefore bear unlimited direct-damages exposure, which fails the fallback's material term of a mutual 12-month-fees cap. We have proposed the smallest workable edit: a new Section 11.5.1 adding a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments made by AbbVie and USD 1,000,000, expressly preserving the existing clause (A)–(D) carve-outs as uncapped and confirming that AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. Two preferred-position sub-elements are noted but not separately flagged: the carve-out list does not expressly name data protection/security or infringement of the other party's IP (though Article 9 and the Article 11 indemnities largely cover this ground). Note also that the exposure here is symmetrical rather than one-sided against us, so this is a deviation on the cap parameter rather than walk-away territory.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' payments and USD 1,000,000) to Section 11.5, preserving the existing carve-outs as uncapped.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement waives indirect damages but contains no aggregate liability cap, so both Parties carry unlimited direct-damages exposure; our position is a mutual cap set at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000. The existing clause (A)–(D) carve-outs (fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, Article 9 confidentiality, Section 5.8 exclusivity and indemnification) remain outside the cap, and AbbVie's payment obligations under Article 6 are not "damages" for cap purposes.

ops.text: Aggregate Cap. Except for the matters described in clauses (A) through (D) of Section 11.5, for which liability is not capped, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by AbbVie to Harpoon under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million United States Dollars (US$1,000,000). AbbVie's obligation to pay amounts that have become due under Article 6 shall not constitute damages for purposes of, and shall not be subject to or count against, the foregoing cap.
